name: CD4066BM96
title: CD4066B quad bilateral CMOS analog switch
summary: Four independent single-pole single-throw CMOS switches in one 14-pin package, each with its own control input. It runs from 3 V to 18 V between VDD and VSS and passes analog or digital signals in either direction anywhere from VSS to VDD. On resistance is 125 Ω typical at 15 V and 470 Ω at 5 V, with 5 Ω typical difference between switches at 15 V; the pinout is that of the CD4016B.

circuits.title: Bidirectional signal switching under digital control
circuits.description: A CD4054B level shifter takes four 0 V / 5 V logic control lines and drives the four CD4066B control inputs with levels swinging between +5 V and -5 V. The CD4066B runs from VDD = 5 V and VSS = -5 V, so each switch passes an analog signal of ±5 V in either direction between its two terminals.

parts.note: level shifter, VDD = 5 V, VSS = 0 V, VEE = -5 V

circuits.title: Four-channel PAM multiplex system
circuits.description: Four analog channels share one line in turn and are separated again at the receiving end. Transmit side: a CD4018B counter, two CD4049B inverters and a CD4001B quad NOR form four select lines from the counter's Q1 and Q2 outputs and their complements; these drive the four controls of a CD4066B whose outputs are tied together on the line, loaded by 10 kΩ to ground. One more switch, with input and control both on the clock, also feeds the line. Receive side: the line clocks a second CD4018B with the same inverter and NOR decoding, and drives, through a CD4049B inverter, the control of a switch the line passes through; that switch feeds a second CD4066B whose four outputs each have 10 kΩ to ground and a low-pass filter to a channel output.
notes: Misprint: U9 output 3 is drawn to CD4066B pin 11; it should read pin 13 (CONTROL A), as on the transmit side.
U11 pins 1, 4 and 11 have no connection; only pin 8 takes the gated line.

equations.name: VDD current capability with separate signal supplies

where.RL: combined external load of all four switches

equations.note: Keeps current from flowing into VDD or the clamp diodes during supply turn-on and turn-off.

operation.text: Each of the four switches is a p-channel and n-channel transistor pair, both turned on or off together by its control input. The n-channel well is tied to the signal input while the switch is on and to VSS while it is off. All p substrates go to VDD, and every control input has the standard CMOS protection network.

A switch is on with its control at VDD (logic 1) and off with its control at VSS (logic 0). Signals may lie anywhere from VSS to VDD. VSS sets the low level and need not be 0 V: with VDD = 5 V and VSS = -5 V the switches pass ±5 V signals.
Control high: the OUT/IN terminal follows the IN/OUT terminal (H gives H, L gives L). Control low: the switch is high impedance whatever the input.

When the signal inputs come from a different source than VDD, the VDD supply must be able to source more than VDD/RL, RL being the total external load on the four switches, so no lasting current or clamping appears at VDD during power-up or power-down.

Where the load current has a VDD part as well as a signal-line part, the drop across a switch must stay at or under 0.8 V (worked out from rON) when current enters pins 1, 4, 8 or 11, or VDD current is drawn. Current entering pins 2, 3, 9 or 10 draws no VDD current through RL.
Keep switch load currents within ±10 mA.

The CMOS outputs have balanced drive. Contention on a shared bus can push currents past the maximum ratings, and the strong drive gives fast edges that can ring into light loads; routing and load conditions are chosen to prevent ringing.

Any supply within the recommended range may be used. Bypass each supply pin close to the pin: 0.1 µF for a single-supply part; 0.01 µF or 0.022 µF per pin where there are several supply pins. A 0.1 µF and a 1 µF in parallel are a common pairing for wider noise rejection.
Unused CMOS inputs must not float: an open input sits at an undefined voltage and leaves operation undefined. Each unused input is tied high or low (VDD or ground), whichever suits its function.

Pin-for-pin compatible with the CD4016B, with much lower on-state resistance that stays nearly constant across the full signal-input range. The CD4016B is the recommended part for sample-and-hold use. Other qualified versions: CD4066B-Q1 (automotive, Q100) and CD4066B-MIL (military, QML).

Analog and digital signal gating and multiplexing, modulators and demodulators, squelch, choppers, commutating switches, A/D and D/A conversion, and setting gain, phase, impedance or frequency from logic.
The part can be damaged by electrostatic discharge and needs normal handling precautions.
